body.x: Semiconductor, automotive and electronics makers need to measure thin films and coatings quickly and accurately, without damaging the sample, across thicknesses that run from under 1 nm to 5 mm.
ThetaMetrisis does it with light reflected from the surface.

ThetaMetrisis S.A., an Athens-based company founded in 2009 as a spin-off from the Institute of Microelectronics at the National Center for Scientific Research "Demokritos," builds optical metrology systems on White Light Reflectance Spectroscopy (WLRS) across the ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared range. At KES 2026, it is exhibiting automated Wafer Mapping systems and its FR-Monitor analysis software, and plans to give Korean stakeholders a preview of its upcoming hyperspectral imaging technology. The company is taking part through the EU Business Hub mission, working alongside Korean partner INA-TECH Co. Ltd.

Its turn-key systems provide real-time, non-destructive characterization of films and coatings for research laboratories and manufacturing lines. International sales account for 95% of its revenue, and the company reports more than 400 active installations in academic laboratories and industrial production lines in 30 countries.

South Korea accounts for 15.8% of ThetaMetrisis's international sales, or an average of EUR 150,000 a year, which the company says mostly reflects single-tool sales to specialized research facilities. It aims to reach EUR 450,000 by 2028 by moving to multi-unit, automated production-line installations, such as its FR-CasScan and FR-InLine systems, at large manufacturers.

Together with INA-TECH, ThetaMetrisis plans to move its technology from research laboratories into high-volume automated production lines in Korea's semiconductor, advanced display and mobility sectors. INA-TECH invited the company's executive and engineering leaders to KES 2026, where the two teams plan to host joint technical demonstrations of the Wafer Mapping system for INA-TECH's network of equipment manufacturers. The company says INA-TECH can provide local service and maintenance support for Korean customers.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
